title: The Morning Call That Told Richard Eu His Family Firm Had Been Sold
conflicts: The slate's 1879 founding by Eu Kong conflicts between the company/NLB/NHB account (medicine shop for opium-using miners, 1873 arrival) and biography-derived accounts (1876 arrival, grocery first, revenue farms that per Wikipedia included opium). Not checkable against the 2009 biography, so the edition switched to Richard Eu's 1989-1993 takeover and buyback and gives the founding only 'by the company's account'. Minor: joined end-1989 (KiniBiz) vs 1990 (Wikipedia); age 40 (Endeavor) vs born 1947; shop counts 170-300.
notes: Episode changed, as RESEARCH-AGENT allows (same company, single documented episode); founder field is Richard Eu (fourth generation, not the founder). Founder quotation 'We have just received a notice of takeover from Lum Chang' is Eu's recollection of the bank's words (Endeavor Malaysia 2022). 'Jealous' uncles attributed to Eu. Wikipedia used once, as supplementary support for the 1990 and 1993 dates.
